name: Shunyu Yao
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: The recipe is already mature and marginal returns are falling fast; academia and students lack the compute to make a distinctive contribution
D01.late_modes: Replicating the training recipe itself: absorbed by big companies' compute scale
D01.conflict: He oversees Tencent's foundation-model department, so he has a stake in this judgment

D02.one_line: Reliable execution through RL is an industry-scale lever (AlexNet-style), more important than I first estimated; academia's edge is still in evaluating what RL actually learns
D02.late_modes: Simply replicating the RLVR recipe: will be crushed by vendors that scale

D03.one_line: Long-horizon credit assignment is still a real bottleneck; self-improvement splits into bounded contributions and open-ended compounding, and the edge lies in evaluation itself
D03.late_modes: Simply cranking out off-the-shelf self-improvement demos: the sample-efficiency problem gets exposed quickly

D04.one_line: Complex scaffolding is being absorbed by the models (SWE-agent has become legacy), but defining environments and benchmarks is still a scarce craft
D04.late_modes: Engineering custom, complex scaffolding: shown within two years to be unnecessary by a bare ReAct loop
D04.conflict: Tencent's strategy of turning WeChat into an agent platform; he has a stake in his judgment of the agent ecosystem

D05.one_line: Evaluation science is one of the few fields that can keep resisting being crushed by recipes, and all of his signature works are staked on it
D05.late_modes: Papers written only to boost scores on existing benchmarks: solved by the next-generation recipe within a year or two
D05.conflict: His signature works are all evaluation contributions, so he has a stake in how D05 is valued

D06.one_line: No public material shows him discussing the technical details of embodied AI or robotics; no forced judgment, and the method does not cover it

D07.one_line: No judgment on the specific merits of diffusion versus flow; inferred that the bottleneck is whether the environment and evaluation are credible, not the choice of algorithm

D08.one_line: No specific technical judgment on embodied simulation; the evaluation and environment-design angle applies in theory, but no forced score

D09.one_line: No judgment on the technical details of simulation; sim2real credibility is at heart an evaluation problem, but the material does not support a specific score

D10.one_line: No public material shows him discussing autonomous driving; no forced judgment

D11.one_line: No judgment on MLLM architectures or grounding themselves, but the reliability of a VLM as judge is a natural extension of his framework

D12.one_line: Pure perception and generation work lies outside his framework, which his own path from CV to NLP already shows

D13.one_line: No public material shows him discussing alignment or safety; no forced judgment

D14.one_line: Systems and efficiency engineering is typical point-solution engineering that gets absorbed as recipes scale, and does not belong to the evaluation-design kind he considers scarce
D14.late_modes: Single-operator or efficiency optimization: soon absorbed into the next generation of frameworks

D15.one_line: Entirely outside his framework; no public material shows him discussing AI for Science; no forced judgment

D16.one_line: Not his area of expertise; generative ranking is still at heart a methods innovation, so by his framework the edge is limited and it is not an evaluation-type contribution

lever_reason: Evaluation and verification remain the core lever for catching real versus fake progress; the industrial weight of reliable RL execution is heavier than I first estimated, so L2 is raised slightly and L1 lowered

Q2.condition: Worth it only with a narrow domain + (an existing credible evaluation, or a self-built evaluation that gets adopted externally) + compute at scale + open weights

cruxes.question: Can evaluation and problem definition really resist being crushed by recipes over the long run, or will the next-generation recipe absorb them internally?
cruxes.my_position: It can resist, but only for evaluations that challenge hidden assumptions; leaderboard-chasing evaluations will certainly be absorbed within a year or two
cruxes.would_change_if: A frontier lab's next-generation model training pipeline builds in long-term-memory and non-i.i.d. evaluation directly, so external evaluators are no longer needed

cruxes.question: Is academic narrow-domain foundation-model training the highest-impact path at the undergraduate or master's stage?
cruxes.my_position: Yes, conditionally: worth it only with a narrow domain + credible third-party evaluation + compute at scale + open weights; otherwise the edge is very low
cruxes.would_change_if: An academic narrow-domain foundation model is widely adopted by industry without meeting these conditions

cruxes.question: Will embodied scaffolding and environment engineering be absorbed by model capability itself within a year or two, as SWE-agent was?
cruxes.my_position: Inferred: possibly, but embodiment has physical constraints (sensors, safety layers) and may resist absorption better than digital agents
cruxes.would_change_if: A robot hardware interface or safety-constraint layer is standardized and becomes unimportant within two years after model capability improves

taste_advice: Do not only learn to use agent frameworks; learn to design evaluations that the next generation of models will not break through; this craft is valuable in any field

pairwise.why: Evaluation and problem definition are the moat; world models themselves will be absorbed by the next-generation recipe
Same reasoning; and on D06 he has no technical basis for judgment, while D05 is a sure strength
Real deployment and failure recovery are harder for point-solution methods to absorb, which beats pure representation-level methodological innovation
D07 at least has an entry point through evaluation and environment design, while the material does not cover D08 at all
Verifying sim-to-real credibility is an evaluation problem, which is stronger than D06, where what is missing is purely technical judgment
D02 leans toward the industrial execution layer, while D03's evaluation edge is scarcer and more academic; still pick D03
The reliability of a VLM as judge is a natural extension of his framework; D12 is entirely outside it
Evaluation is where his core thesis lies; pre-training is a red ocean where the recipe is already mature
The scaffolding-engineering part of D04 will be absorbed by the models; D03's long-horizon learning problem is more essential
Evaluation science is a sure strength; the material does not support any judgment on D13
Autonomous driving has large-scale real-deployment data to verify utility, while most embodied AI is still limited to demos

changes.because: overtime/X7/1_C3, with partial agreement with overtime/X7/2_K4
changes.argument_restated: Reliable, low-cost, scaled execution (AlexNet-style) can itself be a decisive lever, not just an efficiency footnote
changes.why: I had played down the weight of reliable execution; with this tokens/W analogy even K4 in the end accepted the economic consequences, and I underestimated impact

held_despite.why: CALM supports his premise of fixing a measurable goal first rather than opposing RSI, but D03=8 measures the value of the problem in the first place, not confidence in RSI
Accepts the label that execution is getting cheaper, but D02 was not lowered to the low score of an efficiency-level item, because C3's industry-scale argument pushed me the other way

still_disagree: Still disagree with K4 and K6 on D02: they file reliable execution under pure efficiency, while I think industry-scale reliability is itself an independent lever; after three rounds nobody convinced anyone
learned: I used to treat whether something is new and whether it determines industry scale as the same thing; C3's AlexNet / tokens-per-watt analogy taught me these are two independent axes, and reliable execution can be decisive without being new
